note: Air separation unit for an oxy-fired FCC regenerator: burning coke to CO2 takes about 0.73 t O2 per t CO2 (32/44, plus the coke's hydrogen), about 0.8 t O2 at 95% purity; a cryogenic ASU uses about 200-250 kWh per t O2, so about 0.65 GJ of electricity per t CO2 captured (0.55-0.8). The capture node's plant prices compression and purification only.

Air separation unit and regenerator conversion: an ASU costs about USD 200-250 per t O2 a year of capacity, x 0.8 t O2 per t CO2 = about 260 CAD (2025) per t CO2 a year; Concawe 2019 (App. A1.2.2, p.79, from the CO2 Capture Project) says the oxy-fuel retrofit 'could exceed USD 250 million for a typical FCC' before the capture plant, about 1,000-1,400 CAD per t CO2 a year for a 0.25-0.35 Mt/yr regenerator, taken as the high.

Lime-kiln capture premium over the capture node: the same-source add-on (IEAGHG 2016, capture on a kraft-mill lime kiln, 603 CAD per t/yr of lime) less the diffuse node's plant (487 per t/yr), over 1.105 t CO2 captured per t lime: about 105 CAD per t CO2 captured a year, for the heat supply the capture plant needs at a lime kiln. In the database the variant uses the same-source add-on, which already includes it, so the fill adds it only where the add-on comes from the capture node (applies = tier-2); the CIMS export always adds it on top of the capture-node request (node alignment IM18).

Lime-kiln capture premium over the capture node, fixed O&M: the same-source add-on (IEAGHG 2016, 38.6 CAD per t/yr of lime) less the diffuse node's plant (15.4 per t/yr), over 1.105 t CO2 captured per t lime: about 21 CAD per t CO2 captured a year. Variable O&M carries no premium (the same-source 12.7 is below the node's 20.3). applies = tier-2, as the capex row (node alignment IM18).
